correctness.rationale: Proved: rank-one coupling makes the protected Q-annihilated subspaces invariant; positivity plus stationary trace loss and projection-invariance forces any nonzero stationary state to avoid the absorber and every dephaser, and then H-invariance forces the entire support into ker H∩ker P_w∩∩ker P_j=Ran Q. Cesaro compactness excludes residual survival on I-Q; positivity and finite dimensionality yield exponential convergence of full density matrices. Rank and budget are elementary dimension and covering counts once the asymptotic projector is proved. Finite independent Lindblad-superoperator tests checked 168 graph/subset cases, plus four time evolutions; they do not prove all-size validity. Rate-uniformity, diagonal disorder and nonfactorizable couplings are excluded.

value.rationale: Selective dephasing can eliminate coherent trapping, but where noise must be applied is a natural graph-transport design question; the theorem gives a complete all-subset classification, exact per-site survival, and an unexpectedly extensive sharp minimum dephaser cost a+b−3 (with exact (a−1)b optimal placements) for every weighted rank-one bipartite network. These are meaningful structural boundaries rather than an isolated parameter choice or routine numerical interpolation. A strongly connected complete bipartite physical graph still requires noise at all but two nonsink sites for extinction of every dark state; infinitesimal positive rates change eventual absorption but not finite-time transport. No general quantum-network speedup is claimed.
